summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Teleport to a far away structure, such as a woodland mansion or pillager outpost, that may contain naturally generated allays.
2. Look at the chunks near you; are they loading in?
3a. If they aren't loading in, reload chunks using `F3 + A`. 
3b. If they still don't load in, try teleporting closer to the structure.
4a. If the chunks still didn't load in after reloading, you have successfully reproduced this bug.
4b. If they still didn't load in, you may be on the wrong version of Minecraft, so ensure you are using the correct version.
5. To exit if this happens, do not use `F3 + C` or `ALT + F4`. Instead, follow the appropriate method for your operating system to force close the game. 
6. On Windows: Open Task Manager and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary."
7. On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using `kill <process_id>`.
8. On MacOS: In the application, press and hold Command + Option + Shift, then press Esc to confirm force quit. 
9. Observe that the game remains unresponsive, and you cannot save your world.
Observed Behavior:
When teleporting to a location with a structure containing naturally generated allays, the server hangs and fails to load nearby chunks. The F3 debug menu displays the internal server tick at 18ms, indicating that the server is still processing, but no further chunk loading occurs. Attempts to reload chunks using the F3 + A command do not resolve the issue, and the game becomes unresponsive. Although the user can still access the F3 menu and other UI elements, these do not function correctly, meaning commands cannot be executed, and the game does not respond to user inputs.

In some instances, a small number of chunks (between 2 to 8) may load if the player is positioned outside the structure containing the allays. However, if the player attempts to save the world while in this state, the game will hang indefinitely, necessitating a forced crash to exit the application. It is important to note that no data will be saved in this scenario. 

The issue appears to be specific to structures with naturally generated allays, as summoning an allay using the command "/summon allay" or visiting a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays does not trigger this behavior. This indicates a possible bug related to the interaction between the game’s chunk loading mechanics and the allay entities within those structures. 

This behavior has been consistently reproducible under the following conditions:
- The player must teleport a significant distance away from their original location to a structure that contains allays naturally generated.
- The game version must be 22w13a, as this issue may not manifest in other versions or may have been patched in later snapshots. 

Developers should investigate the chunk loading process and the server’s handling of allays in these specific scenarios to identify and address the root cause of the hang.
Expected Behavior: When teleporting to a faraway structure containing naturally generated allays, the game should allow chunks to load normally without causing the server to hang or become unresponsive. Players should be able to access the F3 menu and other UI elements without issues, and commands should function as intended. Chunks should load consistently, enabling players to save their worlds without encountering crashes or data loss. Summoning an allay or visiting structures without naturally generated allays should not trigger any performance problems.
